ABOUT.TITLE: About the company
ABOUT.SUBTITLE: Kazhydrogeology is a specialised organisation for the study and monitoring of groundwater
ABOUT.TEXT: NJSC NHS Kazhydrogeology studies, assesses, monitors and manages the sustainable use of groundwater in Kazakhstan. It carries out state tasks in hydrogeology, water supply, irrigation and the digitalisation of water resources.

WELCOME.GREETING: Dear colleagues, partners and visitors of the website!
WELCOME.TEXT_1: Groundwater is one of Kazakhstan's key strategic resources. Today its importance goes far beyond a traditional source of drinking water supply.
WELCOME.TEXT_2: Our country holds vast hydrogeological potential. Previous generations of Kazakhstani specialists carried out enormous work: territories were explored, deposits were surveyed, an observation network was established, and rich information funds were built up. Our task is not simply to preserve this scientific base, but to complement it with modern research, turning accumulated knowledge into a working resource for the economy and the state.
WELCOME.SUBHEAD_1: New challenges and an integrated approach
WELCOME.TEXT_3: Climate change, shrinking surface water and growing pressure on ecosystems call for a new approach. Groundwater must be seen both as a reserve for national water security and as a driver of sustainable economic development.
WELCOME.TEXT_4: This is exactly the principle underpinning the work of the National Hydrogeological Service Kazhydrogeology. We are restoring an integrated state system for studying, monitoring, protecting and rationally using groundwater.
WELCOME.LIST_INTRO: The scope of this resource is considerably wider than commonly assumed:
WELCOME.LIST:
• Drinking and industrial water supply
• Regular and oasis irrigation, watering of pastures
• Use of geothermal energy
• Development of balneology and health resorts (medicinal-mineral and thermal waters)
• Extraction of valuable components from industrial groundwater
WELCOME.TEXT_5: Economic development does not mean uncontrolled exploitation. Every project must be based on reliable data on reserves, quality and replenishment of aquifers. Our priority is to find the balance between today's needs and preserving resources for future generations.
WELCOME.TEXT_6: We attach particular importance to digitalisation. Archival hydrogeological materials are being converted to digital form and integrated with geoinformation systems (GIS) and modern hydrogeological modelling. This will let the state, business and science obtain objective data for making sound decisions.
WELCOME.TEXT_7: We see our website not only as an information board, but as an open platform for professional dialogue. We invite scientists, government officials, entrepreneurs and international partners to cooperate with us.
WELCOME.TEXT_8: We look forward to joint, productive work for the good of Kazakhstan!

WELCOME.POSITION: Chairman of the Management Board, NJSC National Hydrogeological Service Kazhydrogeology

ACTIVITIES.TITLE: Areas of activity
ACTIVITIES.INTRO: The Service's main purpose is to ensure the rational management of the groundwater resources of the Republic of Kazakhstan: their study, exploration and reserve assessment, monitoring and accounting, digitalisation of management, creation and maintenance of databases and geoinformation systems, liquidation and conservation of ownerless self-flowing and emergency hydrogeological wells — in order to meet the needs of the population and sectors of the economy, as well as monitoring and assessing the reclamation status of irrigated land.

LIST.MONITORING_DESC: Systematic observation of the condition and changes of groundwater resources
LIST.SUPPLY_DESC: Supplying groundwater to communities, agriculture and industry
LIST.MELIORATION_DESC: Monitoring and assessment of the reclamation status of land
LIST.DIGITAL_DESC: Maintaining databases, digitalisation and the use of geographic information systems

ACTIVITIES.FULL_LIST_INTRO: In accordance with the Charter of NJSC NHS Kazhydrogeology, the Service carries out the following activities:

FULL_LIST.ITEM_1: Analysis and assessment of water availability from groundwater resources and reserves to meet the needs of the population and sectors of the economy.
FULL_LIST.ITEM_2: Monitoring and assessment of the reclamation status of irrigated land.
FULL_LIST.ITEM_3: Collecting and consolidating groundwater monitoring data, and its digitalisation and automation.
FULL_LIST.ITEM_4: Prospecting and exploration work and assessment of exploitable groundwater reserves for the domestic and drinking water supply of settlements, irrigation of land, industrial water supply, and agricultural water supply, including watering of pastures.
FULL_LIST.ITEM_5: Prospecting and exploration work and assessment of exploitable reserves of mineral groundwater for sanatorium and spa treatment, thermal waters for heat-power purposes, and industrial waters for extracting useful components.
FULL_LIST.ITEM_6: Regional assessment of various types of groundwater resources, assessment of groundwater contamination sources, substantiation and development of treatment methods, assessment of the suitability of areas for disposing of industrial effluents in deep aquifers, and artificial recharge (storage) of groundwater.
FULL_LIST.ITEM_7: Organising the digitalisation of groundwater resource management: creating databases and geoinformation systems in hydrogeology, geofiltration models and digital mapping systems using remote sensing data.
FULL_LIST.ITEM_9: Participation in maintaining the state water cadastre with respect to groundwater.
FULL_LIST.ITEM_10: State prospecting and assessment of groundwater.
FULL_LIST.ITEM_11: Survey, liquidation and conservation of ownerless self-flowing and emergency hydrogeological wells.
FULL_LIST.ITEM_12: Applied scientific research and development work in hydrogeology and engineering geology.

ABOUT_DETAILS.TITLE: About the company
ABOUT_DETAILS.MISSION: : Securing the country's water safety and the sustainable use of groundwater.
ABOUT_DETAILS.GOAL: Building an effective system for recording, monitoring and managing groundwater resources.
ABOUT_DETAILS.TEXT_1: Kazhydrogeology carries out comprehensive research and monitoring of groundwater across the Republic of Kazakhstan. Our work focuses on studying hydrogeological conditions, assessing reserves and ensuring the sustainable use of water resources.
ABOUT_DETAILS.TEXT_2: The organisation takes an active part in state programmes, conducts applied research and supports projects in water supply, ecology and environmental management.
ABOUT_DETAILS.TEXT_4:
• monitoring of groundwater conditions
• assessment and forecasting of water resources
• protection from contamination and depletion
• adoption of modern water management technologies
• participation in maintaining the state water cadastre
• decommissioning of emergency and abandoned wells
• ensuring the rational use and protection of water resources

MELIORATION.TITLE: Monitoring and assessment of the reclamation status of irrigated land
MELIORATION.SHORT_DESC: Over 50 years of observations of Kazakhstan's irrigated land.
MELIORATION.TEXT_1: Kazakhstan's land reclamation service traces its history back to 1971, when a specialised service for monitoring and assessing the reclamation status of irrigated land was established in Shymkent as part of Glavrissovkhozstroy of the USSR Ministry of Water Management.
MELIORATION.TEXT_2: In the following years the system developed further: the Zhetysu and Kyzylorda hydrogeological-reclamation expeditions were formed. Today this work is carried out by the Almaty, Turkestan and Kyzylorda branches of NJSC National Hydrogeological Service Kazhydrogeology, which monitor irrigated land across the Republic of Kazakhstan.
MELIORATION.MONITORING_INTRO: Specialists carry out a range of field, laboratory and desk studies:
MELIORATION.TEXT_3: Based on the results, an annual assessment of the reclamation status of irrigated land is carried out, thematic maps are produced, and recommendations are developed to prevent waterlogging and salinisation, improve land condition and make rational use of water resources.
MELIORATION.TEXT_4: Over the years a substantial archive of hydrogeological, soil-reclamation and cartographic materials has been built up, making it possible to track long-term changes in the condition of irrigated areas.
MELIORATION.TEXT_5: Today the National Hydrogeological Service is working to preserve and digitise this data, develop a unified information base, and apply GIS technology, remote sensing and modern monitoring methods.
MELIORATION.GOAL_TEXT: to move from simply recording the current state to the timely detection and forecasting of negative processes, preserving the productivity of irrigated land and the effective use of Kazakhstan's water resources.

DIGITALIZATION.SHORT_DESC: A unified digital platform, automated monitoring and digital modelling of aquifers.
DIGITALIZATION.SEC1_TITLE: A unified digital platform for groundwater
DIGITALIZATION.SEC1_LIST:
• creating a unified geoinformation platform for Kazakhstan's groundwater;
• combining data on wells, deposits, reserves, the cadastre, monitoring, water users and geological funds in a single system.
DIGITALIZATION.SEC2_LIST:
• converting geological funds and archival materials into digital form;
• creating a unified digital groundwater cadastre.
DIGITALIZATION.SEC6_LIST:
• integration with the water and land cadastres, the hydrometeorological service, geology authorities and regional administrations;
• a shared information space and data exchange.
DIGITALIZATION.RESULT_TEXT: moving from scattered archival and departmental data to a unified digital system for managing groundwater: from exploration and monitoring to the cadastre, modelling, forecasting and management decisions.

bekniyaz.NAME: Bolat Bekniyaz
bekniyaz.DESCRIPTION:
Graduated from the Kazakh Polytechnic Institute named after V.I. Lenin, the Academy of Public Administration under the President of the Republic of Kazakhstan, Lomonosov Moscow State University, and Taraz State University named after M. Dulati.

His professional career is linked to geology, water resources, research work and public administration.

He began his career as an engineer at the K. Satpayev Institute of Geological Sciences of the Academy of Sciences of the Kazakh SSR, later moving into research work there.

He has many years of experience in public administration, having held senior positions in government bodies in the fields of natural resources, environmental protection and water resource management. He also has experience in research and sector-specific work at water-sector organisations.

His professional experience spans state water policy, the management and protection of water resources, the development of the water management sector, and scientific and institutional support for the water sector.

He currently serves as Chair of the Management Board of NJSC National Hydrogeological Service Kazhydrogeology.

ibraev.NAME: Dair Ibrayev
ibraev.DESCRIPTION:
He began his career in hydrogeology, working as a hydrogeology technician and hydrogeology engineer at specialised hydrogeological organisations.

A significant part of his professional experience is linked to the public administration system in the field of geology. At the Geology Committee he advanced from expert and chief expert to head of department, working on hydrogeology and state regulation of the sector.

He has experience in expert consulting work as well as teaching specialised disciplines in hydrogeology.

His professional experience spans practical hydrogeology, the study and use of groundwater, public administration and regulation in the field of geology, and the training of specialised personnel.

He currently serves as First Deputy Chair of the Management Board of NJSC National Hydrogeological Service Kazhydrogeology.

vakasova.NAME: Guldanam Vakasova
vakasova.DESCRIPTION:
Graduated from the K.I. Satpayev Kazakh National Technical University with a degree in Hydrogeology and Engineering Geology.

Earned a master's degree in agricultural sciences from the Kazakh National Agrarian University, majoring in Water Resources and Water Use.

Continued her studies at the Warsaw University of Life Sciences in environmental engineering, housing management and energy, earning an international master's degree in environmental engineering.

Her professional career is linked to hydrogeology and water management. She has practical and managerial experience in hydrogeological research, the operation of water management systems, water use and hydrometry. She worked within the RSE Kazvodkhoz system, progressing from hydraulic engineer to head of a department responsible for water use and hydrometry. She has also worked as a geological engineer at a hydrogeological organisation.

She currently serves as Deputy Chair of the Management Board of NJSC National Hydrogeological Service Kazhydrogeology.
